title: A Signal From Space Was So Strange, A Scientist Wrote 'Wow!' Next To It
description:
In 1977, a radio telescope picked up a signal so unusual that the astronomer reviewing it circled the reading and wrote 'Wow!' in the margin. Decades later, it's still debated.

#shorts #sciencefacts #space #didyouknow

scenes.text: In August of 1977, a radio telescope in Ohio picked up a signal so unusual that the astronomer reviewing the printout circled it and wrote a single word in the margin: Wow!
The signal lasted seventy two seconds, was far stronger than the background noise around it, and came from the direction of the constellation Sagittarius.
It was never detected again, despite astronomers pointing telescopes back at that exact patch of sky many times since.
In 2017, a research team proposed an explanation: two previously undiscovered comets passing through that same patch of sky, since comets can give off a faint hydrogen radio signal of their own.
That explanation is genuinely disputed, though -- other astronomers have pointed out problems with the comets' actual position and brightness that don't fully line up.
So the honest answer, decades later, is that nobody has definitively explained it. The comet idea is a real, published theory, not a settled one.
If a signal like that showed up again tomorrow, do you think it would turn out to be something natural, or something else?
